source.title: Rho-1: Not All Tokens Are What You Need
source.authors: Zheng-Wen Lin; Zhibin Gou; Yeyun Gong; Xiao Liu; Yelong Shen; Ruochen Xu; Chen Lin; Yu-Jiu Yang; Jian Jiao; Nan Duan; Wei-Zhu Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether downstream accuracy relates to pretraining loss, using selected- and unselected-token loss rather than the scaling-law measurements in the original studies. It does not test parameter, data, or compute scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work as background but does not sweep model size, training tokens, or compute to fit or test scaling laws, test extrapolation, or find compute-optimal allocations. It does report a loss–downstream-accuracy relationship using selected and unselected token losses, and token-level validation-loss trajectory categories. General benchmark gains from SLM versus CLM are not scaling-law results and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Rho-1 is a token-selection method paper. It sweeps no parameters, tokens or compute to fit or extrapolate scaling laws. Its only loss-to-accuracy analysis (Fig. 7, App. F) uses five checkpoints of its own SLM run and loss on token subsets its method defines. That supports the method rather than testing V6's claim that downstream performance tracks scale or overall pretraining loss. It is a related construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that tokens have heterogeneous loss dynamics and that SLM, which trains on high excess-loss tokens, improves data efficiency and downstream math and general performance. They also say the all-token loss need not fall for downstream gains. They make no claims about the catalogued scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes selective token training; it does not reproduce or adapt the original scaling-law measurement procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that selected- versus unselected-token loss has a different relationship with downstream accuracy; it also examines token-selection ratios, but those results do not test the catalogued scaling-law versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under selective training, few-shot GSM8k/MATH accuracy rises across checkpoints as selected-token loss falls, while unselected-token loss rises (Fig. 7). The authors fit Acc=log(aL+c) but give no parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy tracks loss on target-aligned tokens rather than loss on all tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: In Tinyllama-1B continual pretraining on OpenWebMath, validation tokens split into H→L 26%, L→L 51%, H→H 11% and L→H 12% loss trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-token loss trajectories are heterogeneous even while aggregate loss decreases smoothly.

record.problems: The authors state that budget constraints limited verification to models of <=7B parameters and datasets of <100B tokens. The loss–accuracy relationship is presented for selected-token and unselected-token loss in one training setting; numerical fit parameters and uncertainty estimates are not stated, and plotted values are not tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Benchmark comparisons of SLM against CLM and token-selection-ratio ablations do not test the scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: Downstream accuracy versus model scale, or versus overall all-token pretraining loss, across models or runs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is dropped. The evidence is five checkpoints from the study's own method, uses token-subset losses, gives no fit parameters, and states a fitted sign (a>0) that conflicts with the plotted trend. Scaling laws appear only as background (Intro, App. B.4). The scalability limitation (<=7B, <100B tokens) is a statement about the method, not a scaling result.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law scaling of held-out pretraining loss with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of substantially larger runs from small-run fits.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation trends.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds across modalities or other training regimes.

The study relates downstream accuracy to selected- and unselected-token loss in a particular training setting; it does not test scaling-based predictability or the relationship to overall pretraining loss across models.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices.

rows.subject: R HO -1 / Tinyllama-1B
rows.operation_detail: Relates average GSM8k and MATH accuracy to selected-token loss at training checkpoints.

conditions.value: GSM8k and MATH average few-shot accuracy

rows.measure: Downstream accuracy as a function of selected-token loss
rows.value: The paper proposes Acc(L) = log(a * L + c); for selected-token loss, a > 0. Numerical fit values are not stated; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: Appendix F describes fitting this relationship to the plotted points. The row captures the reported association, not a general scaling law or a test of overall pretraining loss.
rows.check: The measure is loss on SLM-selected tokens within one SLM run (5 checkpoints), not overall pretraining loss or scale. No fit values are given. The stated sign (a>0 in log(aL+c)) implies accuracy rises with loss, which contradicts Fig. 7, where accuracy rises as selected loss falls from 0.98 to 0.86. So the reported fit can't be read.

rows.subject: R HO -1 / Tinyllama-1B
rows.operation_detail: Relates average GSM8k and MATH accuracy to unselected-token loss at training checkpoints.

conditions.value: GSM8k and MATH average few-shot accuracy

rows.measure: Downstream accuracy as a function of unselected-token loss
rows.value: The paper proposes Acc(L) = log(a * L + c); for unselected-token loss, a < 0. Numerical fit values are not stated; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: Appendix F describes fitting this relationship to the plotted points. This is a token-subset loss association, not a scaling-law fit.
rows.check: The measure is loss on unselected tokens within the same SLM run, not overall pretraining loss. Accuracy rises while this loss rises (3.50 to 3.66). No fit values are given.

rows.subject: Tinyllama-1B

rows.measure: Share of tokens classified as H→L (loss decreases from high to low)
rows.note: This is a token-category share, not a test of a power-law fit for aggregate held-out loss.
rows.check: Token-trajectory category share from a CLM continual-pretraining run; not a scaling-law measure.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected- and unselected-token loss versus average GSM8k and MATH few-shot accuracy at the reported checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: The authors report fitting an accuracy–loss relationship, with opposite signs for the selected- and unselected-token fits; see R1 and R2. This supports predictability only for these token-subset loss measures and this setting.
